description: Resolve all warnings in src/RetroPickDoorwayV1.sol and the three Doorway test files. These are the clearest fix-in-code cases: add missing events/zero-checks on the cross-chain migration doorway (which handles fees and access control), and update tests to capture block.timestamp before vm.warp. Independent of the other source-file features; can be done first among the fix features.
steps: READ src/RetroPickDoorwayV1.sol fully first, then apply per-warning judgment as follows.

missing-events-access-control at lines 421 (setRelayer), 427 (setGuardian), 445 (transferOwnership): These setters change access-control state. Note setRelayer/setGuardian ALREADY emit RelayerUpdated/GuardianUpdated with old->new BEFORE assignment. Verify the events exist and are emitted; if the lint still fires it is because the emit is treated as not covering the assignment - confirm the emit references both old and new value and is on the same setter. transferOwnership (line ~445) currently has NO event: add an `OwnershipTransferred(address indexed previousOwner, address indexed newOwner)` event declaration and emit it in transferOwnership before/at the assignment (emit old owner and newOwner). If setRelayer/setGuardian genuinely already emit and the warning persists, treat as the linter wanting the emit adjacent - keep the existing emit; only if it still warns after building, add a targeted `// forge-lint: disable-next-line(missing-events-access-control)` with justification that the event is emitted one line above. Prefer real events over suppression.

missing-events-arithmetic at line 435 (setFee -> migrationFeeBps): setFee already emits FeeUpdated(migrationFeeBps, newFeeBps) before assignment. Verify the event is emitted; migrationFeeBps is used in fee arithmetic (calculateFee). If the event already covers it, the warning should clear; if it persists, ensure the emit is in the same function immediately before the assignment. Do not remove existing events.

missing-zero-check in constructor at line 121 (_treasury, _relayer, _guardian) and in setRelayer (418), setGuardian (424): Add `require(x != address(0), "RetroPickDoorwayV1: zero <name>")` (or a custom revert consistent with the file's style - the file uses require strings) for each address parameter: _treasury, _relayer, _guardian in the constructor; newRelayer in setRelayer; newGuardian in setGuardian. Match the existing require-string style already used in transferOwnership ("RetroPickDoorwayV1: zero owner").

block-timestamp at line 367 (cancelMigration: `require(block.timestamp >= migration.createdAt + CANCELLATION_DELAY ...)`): This is a coarse, minute/hour-scale cancellation delay where miner timestamp manipulation (a few seconds) is harmless and cannot bypass the delay meaningfully. This is a false positive by design. Add immediately above line 367:
  `// block-timestamp: CANCELLATION_DELAY is coarse (minutes+); miner timestamp drift of seconds cannot bypass the lock.`
  `// forge-lint: disable-next-line(block-timestamp)`

environment-read-across-mutation in test/integration/RetroPickDoorwayE2E.t.sol (lines 64, 71, 131), test/unit/RetroPickDoorwayBase.t.sol (line 73), test/unit/RetroPickDoorwayLifecycle.t.sol (line 149): Replace bare `block.timestamp` reads that are reused across a `vm.warp(...)` with `vm.getBlockTimestamp()` as the linter recommends. For each flagged site: where the test reads block.timestamp (e.g. building an Attestation struct timestamp, or inside a vm.warp expression), use vm.getBlockTimestamp(). READ each test file around the flagged lines first to make the minimal correct change; ensure the tests still express the same intent (attestation timestamp = current block time; warp forward by a delta). Do NOT change test logic beyond swapping the timestamp source.
After edits, run `forge build --force` and confirm ZERO warnings remain that point at src/RetroPickDoorwayV1.sol or any test/ file.
Run `forge test` and confirm the Doorway unit/integration tests still pass (no regressions from the added zero-checks/events or timestamp source change).
acceptance_criteria: No warnings from `forge build --force` reference src/RetroPickDoorwayV1.sol.
No environment-read-across-mutation warnings reference any test/ file.
Each address parameter in the constructor, setRelayer, and setGuardian has a zero-address check.
transferOwnership emits an ownership-transfer event (or existing events cover the access-control setters).
block-timestamp at cancelMigration is suppressed with a specific justification comment, not deleted logic.
forge test passes with no new failures versus the FEAT-001 baseline.
verification: forge build --force 2>&1 | grep -E 'RetroPickDoorwayV1.sol|test/' | grep -c warning returns 0
forge test passes for the Doorway suites with no regressions vs baseline
findings:
All 11 in-scope warnings resolved; forge build --force has zero warnings referencing src/RetroPickDoorwayV1.sol or any test/ file (total warnings dropped 93 -> 78). forge test = 45 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped (matches FEAT-001 baseline). Per-warning outcome:
- missing-zero-check (constructor 121 x3): FIXED IN CODE. Added require(_treasury/_relayer/_guardian != address(0), "RetroPickDoorwayV1: zero <name>").
- missing-zero-check (setRelayer 418, setGuardian 424): FIXED IN CODE. Added require(newRelayer/newGuardian != address(0), ...).
- missing-events-access-control (transferOwnership): FIXED IN CODE. Declared event OwnershipTransferred(address indexed previousOwner, address indexed newOwner) in IRetroPickDoorwayV1.sol and emit it (old owner, newOwner) immediately before assignment.
- missing-events-access-control (setRelayer, setGuardian) and missing-events-arithmetic (setFee): existing RelayerUpdated/GuardianUpdated/FeeUpdated events already emit old->new immediately before assignment and were verified/kept. The linter's heuristic still fired because it does not recognize the adjacent emit as covering the assignment; SUPPRESSED WITH JUSTIFICATION using per-line // forge-lint: disable-next-line(...) plus a concrete reason comment on each of the four assignment lines (relayer, guardian, owner, migrationFeeBps). Real events preferred; suppression only for the linter false positive.
- block-timestamp (cancelMigration ~367): SUPPRESSED WITH JUSTIFICATION. CANCELLATION_DELAY is coarse (minutes+); seconds-scale miner timestamp drift cannot bypass the lock. Added the two-line justified disable comment; logic unchanged.
- environment-read-across-mutation (E2E 64/71/131, Base 73, Lifecycle 149): FIXED IN CODE. Replaced bare block.timestamp reads that are reused across vm.warp with vm.getBlockTimestamp() per the linter help; test intent unchanged (attestation timestamp = current block time; warp forward by delta). E2E lines 138/154 were NOT flagged and left untouched. No source files outside Doorway/interface and the three test files were modified. Not committed/pushed per instructions handled by this feature's own commit below.
